narrative: Traces the cultural history of labeling unfamiliar harmonics as forbidden or wrong — from the medieval diabolus in musica through equal temperament's systematic exclusion of the seventh harmonic — and argues that the bent notes of blues, jazz, barbershop, and global vocal traditions were not departures from correct tuning but approaches toward consonances older and simpler than the equal-tempered grid could reach. The chapter connects the mathematical irrationality of the Pythagorean comma to the same structural crisis as the incommensurable diagonal, frames the keyboard as a narrow transduction channel that discards what the voice can keep, and reads Western musicology's vocabulary of error as a framework defending its own cartoon against the physics it had suppressed.
